description: C++ Templates and Standard Template Library: Vector, Stack, Queue, Map, Set and Iterators

questions.questionText: What is the main purpose of templates in C++?
questions.optionA: To write generic code that can work with different data types
questions.explanation: Templates allow programmers to write generic code that can operate with different data types.

questions.questionText: Which keyword is commonly used to declare a template?
questions.explanation: The template keyword is used to introduce a template declaration.

questions.questionText: Which keyword can be used to declare a type parameter in a template?
questions.explanation: Both typename and class can be used to declare type parameters in a template.

questions.questionText: Which is a valid function template declaration?
questions.optionB: template T add(T a, T b)
questions.optionC: template <typename T> T add(T a, T b)
questions.explanation: template <typename T> introduces the type parameter T for the function template.

questions.questionText: What is STL in C++?
questions.explanation: STL stands for Standard Template Library and provides reusable containers, algorithms and iterators.

questions.questionText: Which STL container stores elements in a dynamic contiguous sequence?
questions.explanation: std::vector is a dynamic array-like container whose elements are stored contiguously.

questions.questionText: Which header is required for std::vector?
questions.explanation: The vector container is defined in the <vector> header.

questions.questionText: Which function is commonly used to add an element at the end of a vector?
questions.explanation: push_back() adds an element to the end of a vector.

questions.questionText: Which function returns the number of elements currently stored in a vector?
questions.explanation: The size() function returns the current number of elements in a vector.

questions.questionText: Which STL container follows the LIFO principle?
questions.explanation: A stack follows Last In, First Out (LIFO).

questions.questionText: Which function adds an element to a stack?
questions.explanation: The push() function adds an element to the top of a stack.

questions.questionText: Which function removes the top element from a stack?
questions.explanation: The pop() function removes the top element from a stack.

questions.questionText: Which function returns the top element of a stack without removing it?
questions.explanation: The top() function returns a reference to the top element without removing it.

questions.questionText: Which STL container follows the FIFO principle?
questions.explanation: A queue follows First In, First Out (FIFO).

questions.questionText: Which function adds an element to the back of a queue?
questions.explanation: The push() function adds an element to the back of a std::queue.

questions.questionText: Which function removes the front element from a queue?
questions.explanation: The pop() function removes the front element from a std::queue.

questions.questionText: Which STL container stores key-value pairs?
questions.explanation: std::map stores elements as key-value pairs.

questions.questionText: In a std::map, are keys unique?
questions.explanation: Each key in std::map is unique. For duplicate keys, std::multimap can be used.

questions.questionText: Which STL container stores unique elements in sorted order by default?
questions.explanation: std::set stores unique elements and maintains them in sorted order by default.

questions.questionText: What happens when a duplicate value is inserted into a std::set?
questions.explanation: A std::set stores only unique values, so duplicate insertion does not add another copy.

questions.questionText: What is an iterator in STL?
questions.optionA: A special data type for strings only
questions.optionB: An object used to traverse elements of a container
questions.explanation: Iterators provide a way to access and traverse elements of STL containers.

questions.questionText: Which function returns an iterator pointing to the first element of a container?
questions.explanation: The begin() member function returns an iterator referring to the first element.

questions.questionText: Which function returns an iterator representing the position after the last element?
questions.explanation: The end() iterator represents the position just after the last element.

questions.questionText: What is the output? vector<int> v = {10, 20, 30}; cout << v[1];
questions.explanation: Vector indexing starts from 0, so v[1] refers to the second element, which is 20.

questions.questionText: Which statement correctly creates a vector containing three integers 10, 20 and 30?
questions.explanation: Initializer-list syntax vector<int> v = {10, 20, 30}; creates a vector with those three elements.
